outcome: Measure the DataSpace scenario against MADR 0012, which separated what a deliverable carries (columns) from what it is organized by (order_by, rows.one_per), and record whether the prediction holds that early declarations stop carrying the sort or grain key
criteria: task_44 and task_329 each run three times through the OpenCode container host with the informed declaration framing, the runner's defaults, and every run is recorded

agent_harness/scenarios/dataspace/README.md gains a new dated section at the front of the measurement sections, titled for MADR 0012, in the format of the existing sections: a summary comparison table, a per-run table, and prose on what happened
the per-run table records, for every run, whether order_by and rows/one_per were used and which keys they named, beside the existing per-run columns
the new section states in plain words whether the MADR 0012 prediction held, reports the result as it came out, and notes that six runs is a small sample
framing.py, the MCP tool registry and all backend code are unchanged by this outcome

dispositions.note: the section is at the front of the measurement sections, dated 2026-09-09, with a summary comparison table against the 2026-09-02 OpenCode container arm, a per-run table, and prose

note: Six OpenCode container runs on task_44 and task_329, informed framing, runner defaults, freshly built image; every run completed on its own, none hit the 900 s timeout and none failed for an infrastructure reason. The MADR 0012 prediction did not hold: five of six runs named an organizing key in order_by or one_per, but only one narrowed columns to the payload, and in four runs the same key sits in both lists at once. Official went 2/3 to 1/3 on task_44 and stayed 0/3 on task_329; all five failures are column_count_mismatch on the sort or grain key. The one run that moved the key out passed, and the backend's sort-then-project step worked as 0012 describes. Six runs is a small sample and the section says so. Recorded as it came out, no reruns. framing.py, the MCP tool registry and the backend are untouched; the only repository change is the new README section. A local .env path was corrected (dataset -> datasets); .env is gitignored and is not repository content.
